Q: How can I create a database for a MongoDB container on startup? A:

Given this .env file:

DB_NAME=foo
DB_USER=bar
DB_PASSWORD=baz

And this mongo-init.sh file:

mongo --eval "db.auth('$MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME', '$MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD'); db = db.getSiblingDB('$DB_NAME'); db.createUser({ user: '$DB_USER', pwd: '$DB_PASSWORD', roles: [{ role: 'readWrite', db: '$DB_NAME' }] });"

This docker-compose.yml file will create the administrator database and administrator user, authenticate as the administrator user, create the real database, and add the real user:

version: '3'

services:
#  app:
#    build: .
#    env_file: .env
#    environment:
#      DB_HOST: 'mongodb://mongodb'

  mongodb:
    image: mongo:4
    environment:
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME: admin-user # change this
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD: admin-password # change this
      DB_NAME: $DB_NAME
      DB_USER: $DB_USER
      DB_PASSWORD: $DB_PASSWORD
    ports:
      - "27017:27017"
    volumes:
      - db-data:/data/db
      - ./mongo-init.sh:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/mongo-init.sh

volumes:
  db-data:

Q: Weird html rendering anomaly A:

The issue is your HTML. input tags aren't supposed to have an open and close.

To achieve what you're trying to achieve with:

<input type="hidden" name="id">{{ id }}</input>

You should instead do:

<input type="hidden" name="id" value="{{ id }}">

EDIT: spec if you're interested: http://www.w3.org/TR/html401/interact/forms.html#h-17.4

Q: Merging the headers then concatenate the records of a huge number of text files A:

Taking a completely different tack by using good ol' xargs, head and grep to set-process the files ...

As with my other answer I'll use jhnc's 32 x 635MB data set; this leads to the creation of 32 files named {1..32}.vcf.

General approach:

  • collect a list of file names, sort as needed; with a sorted list of files in hand ...
  • head -n X | grep '^#' - where X is sufficiently large enough to insure to capture all header rows; in the case of our test files there are 17 header lines so we'll play it safe and pick X=20; this approach allows us to abort reading the rest of the file once we have our header rows
  • cat | xargs grep -hv '^#' - extract the data rows

The actual code:

find . -name '[0-9]*.vcf' | sort -V > vcf_file_list

{
    while read -r fname
    do
        head -n 20 "$fname" | grep '^#'
    done < vcf_file_list

    cat vcf_file_list | xargs grep -hv '^#'
} > vcf.out

Taking for a test spin against out test data:

real    0m22.221s
user    0m6.591s
sys     0m13.427s

That's about half the time of my reduced-regex awk script (42.484s) and about 1/3 the time of my original regex-all-rows awk script (1m18.172s).

Q: Sort a column of data to align cells with a separate "key" column? A:

try:

=INDEX(IFNA(VLOOKUP(A2:A; Sheet1!B:B; 1; )))

where Sheet1!B:B is your DATA column
